text: A spectral sequence is said to ___ at $E_2$ when all differentials $d_r$ vanish for $r\geq 2$, so that $E_2=E_\infty$.
explanation: When every $d_r=0$ for $r\geq 2$ the pages never change past $E_2$, giving $E_2=E_\infty$; the chapter calls this degenerating (or collapsing) at $E_2$. This is the most convenient case, since the input page then already delivers the associated graded of the answer.
